title: Teachers and colleagues: Red Callender, Buddy Collette, Phil Moore
summary: Callender, Collette and Phil Moore's arranging lessons (synthetic violin sound with French horn); Dizzy's debt to Bird.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I think I got (inaudible) by everything. I was influenced by my teacher, Red Calendar. (Inaudible) Buddy Collette inspired me a whole lot, coming up together with him. And Phil Moore. I studied with him, composition. No, I studied with him arranging. Gave me my first organ. That's why I started using (inaudible) organ. And I was writing some things out for him, too. I don't know if he ever used them or not, but he asked me to write something. He said, "How would you -- if you had a record date where they told you the strings were limited? How would you get a full sound?" I said, "I don't know; I'd probably use trombone. That's close -- (inaudible) the French horn." Says, "So write me out" -- what was that word he used? Synthetic violin sound. Where you utilize the French horn to play those long melodies down low. See, it's snowing out. Shit. you know, Man, how can you be influenced by Dizzy Gillespie when he's playing like Charlie Parker? And you played with all of them, and Bud Powell, even. They all were trying to play 'Bout time to cut that thing off, isn't it? (inaudible) Bird. (inaudible) number machine up top there. There's a So you know what number to cut off on. (Etc, etc.)
